group.title: Food and cooking
sources: Words and CEFR levels chosen by the authors from general knowledge of English; meanings, examples and sentences are original

Word-list licences checked 2026-10-25: CEFR-J Wordlist 1.5 (Tono Laboratory, TUFS; free with citation, A1-B2) and NGSL/NAWL (CC BY-SA 4.0) were not copied; Oxford 3000 and English Vocabulary Profile terms were not confirmed, so they were not used

words.meaning: To heat water or food until it bubbles.
wrong: I boil the water in the freezer.

words.meaning: To cook food in hot oil.
wrong: I fry eggs in cold water.

words.meaning: To cook bread or cakes in an oven.
wrong: I bake the cake in the fridge.

words.meaning: A list of food and steps to cook a dish.
wrong: A recipe is a plate you eat from.

words.meaning: One of the foods you use to make a dish.
examples: Flour is the main {ingredient} in bread.
wrong: An ingredient is the oven you use to cook.

words.meaning: A metal pot with a handle, for cooking.
wrong: I drink tea from a frying pan at the café.

words.meaning: A deep round dish for soup or cereal.
wrong: I eat soup from a flat knife.

words.meaning: A list of the food you can order in a restaurant.
wrong: The menu is the person who cooks the food.

words.meaning: A person who brings food to tables in a restaurant.
wrong: The waiter is a customer who never works.

words.meaning: Sweet food you eat after the main meal.
wrong: We had dessert before breakfast as the first course.

words.meaning: A small amount of food between meals.
examples: I have an apple as a {snack}.
wrong: A snack is a very large dinner with five courses.

words.meaning: Food that you eat at one time, like lunch.
wrong: A meal is a drink of water.

words.meaning: Tasting very good.
wrong: The cake was delicious, so nobody wanted it.

words.meaning: Recently made or picked; not old.
wrong: The fish is fresh, so it is two weeks old.

words.meaning: Having a hot, strong taste.
wrong: The soup is spicy, so it has no flavor at all.

words.meaning: Having a sharp taste like a lemon.
wrong: Sugar is very sour.

words.meaning: Having a strong, sharp taste that is not sweet.
wrong: Honey is bitter.

words.meaning: Not cooked.
wrong: The meat is raw because we cooked it for hours.

words.meaning: A white powder made from grain, used for bread and cakes.
examples: Mix the {flour} with eggs and milk.
wrong: Flour is a hot drink.

words.meaning: A soft yellow food made from cream.
wrong: Butter is made from wood.

words.meaning: A thick liquid from plants, used for cooking.
examples: Fry the onions in a little {oil}.
wrong: I drink a glass of oil with breakfast.

words.meaning: A hot powder that you put on food; or a red or green vegetable.
wrong: Pepper is a sweet fruit you eat for dessert.

words.meaning: A liquid food made by boiling meat or vegetables.
wrong: Soup is a hard food you cut with a knife.

words.meaning: Two pieces of bread with food between them.
examples: I had a cheese {sandwich} for lunch.
wrong: A sandwich is a kind of drink.

words.meaning: A dish of raw vegetables such as lettuce.
wrong: A salad is a hot cake with cream.

words.meaning: The parts of an animal that people eat.
examples: I don’t eat {meat}; I’m a vegetarian.
wrong: Vegetarians eat a lot of meat.

words.meaning: A round vegetable that grows under the ground.
wrong: A potato grows at the top of a tall tree.

words.meaning: A soft red fruit used in salads.
wrong: A tomato is a kind of bread.

words.meaning: A round vegetable with a strong smell that makes you cry.
wrong: An onion is a kind of sweet cake.

words.meaning: A round fruit with red or green skin.
examples: An {apple} a day is good for you.
wrong: An apple is a kind of meat.

words.meaning: A long curved fruit with yellow skin.
wrong: A banana is a round red vegetable.

words.meaning: The liquid from fruit.
wrong: Juice is a hard fruit you cut with a knife.

words.meaning: A hot drink made with leaves and water.
examples: Would you like a cup of {tea}?
wrong: Tea is a kind of cheese.

words.meaning: A sweet food baked from flour, sugar and eggs.
examples: We made a {cake} for her birthday.
wrong: A cake is a salty soup.

words.meaning: A sweet brown food made from cocoa.
wrong: Chocolate is a green vegetable.

words.meaning: The flavor that food has in your mouth.
wrong: Taste is what you hear with your ears.

words.meaning: To put different things together.
wrong: I mixed the eggs and flour, so they stayed apart.

words.meaning: A person who does not eat meat or fish.
wrong: A vegetarian eats meat at every meal.

words.meaning: Wanting to drink.
examples: I’m {thirsty}; can I have some water?
wrong: I’m thirsty because I just drank three bottles of water.

words.meaning: To make something warm or hot.
examples: {Heat} the milk, but don’t boil it.
wrong: I heat the soup in the freezer.
